narrative.summary: Jordan governs AI through cabinet-approved policy and soft law led by the Ministry of Digital Economy and Entrepreneurship (MoDEE); there is no AI-specific law. The Jordan AI Policy 2020 (Cabinet Decision No. 659) created a National Ministerial Committee for AI and called for an ethics charter, a sandbox and legal review, and the AI Strategy and Implementation Plan 2023–2027 turns this into 68 projects across priority sectors. The National AI Code of Ethics (2022), which the Cabinet circulated to all government bodies for compliance, is the main responsible-AI instrument. Binding obligations come from the Personal Data Protection Law No. 24 of 2023 (in force March 2024), which covers profiling, and, for banks, the Central Bank of Jordan's AI Framework (July 2025). The Digital Transformation Strategy 2026–2028 makes data and AI a core axis of government digitalisation.

instruments.summary: Jordan's first AI policy, setting the government's direction for AI across economic sectors under five pillars: governance, legislative and regulatory environment, digital infrastructure, business and investment environment, and capacity building. It creates a National Ministerial Committee for AI chaired by the Minister of Digital Economy, requires MoDEE to report annually and review the policy at least every four years, and calls for a national AI ethics charter, a regulatory sandbox and a review of government procurement rules to ease AI adoption.

instruments.summary: Five-year national AI strategy with five objectives: building AI skills, encouraging AI research, improving the AI investment and entrepreneurship environment, ensuring a legislative and regulatory environment for safe AI deployment, and applying AI tools to raise public-sector and priority-sector efficiency. Its implementation plan lists 68 projects across sectors such as government services, health, education, energy, water, agriculture, transport, finance and cybersecurity. Implementation is supervised by the National Council for Entrepreneurship and a MoDEE strategy unit, with a steering committee of government, private-sector and academic representatives.

instruments.summary: Jordan's general data protection law, binding on controllers and processors of personal data inside and outside the Kingdom. It requires prior consent or another legal basis for processing, defines profiling as automated processing to identify a person's trends, preferences or behaviour, and gives data subjects rights including to object to processing and profiling that is unnecessary, excessive or discriminatory. It creates a Personal Data Protection Council and a regulatory unit in MoDEE, and gave existing processors one year after entry into force to comply.

instruments.summary: Central Bank framework for AI used by CBJ-regulated banking institutions, whether developed in-house, procured or outsourced. It sets expectations on AI governance and oversight with a risk-based approach, ethical principles (fairness, explainability, bias mitigation) and customers' right to opt out of automated decisions where appropriate, data privacy and quality, secure development with validation, testing, monitoring and human oversight, AI incident response and business continuity, and third-party risk management.

instruments.official_title: Regulatory Sandbox Framework (FinTech and Innovation Regulatory Sandbox – JoRegBox)
instruments.current_status: Technology-neutral: covers all innovative digital financial solutions; AI is not named explicitly. Recorded because it is the only operating regulatory sandbox in Jordan and AI-based financial solutions fall within its scope of 'innovative digital solutions'.
instruments.summary: Sets the rules of the Central Bank's FinTech and Innovation Regulatory Sandbox: objectives, principles, eligible applicants (licensed banks, fintech startups inside or outside Jordan, university- and government-owned fintechs), eligible activities (banking, insurance, payments, lending, RegTech, SupTech, RiskTech), admission criteria and the stages of testing, normally up to six months. It is technology-neutral and does not refer to AI specifically.

coverage_audit.no_material_found_note: National sources in Jordan were searched in Arabic and English, including the digital economy ministry, the official gazette index, the Legislation and Opinion Bureau, the cybersecurity centre, the telecom regulator, the standards body, the central bank, the procurement department, each ministry and the consultation portal. No AI-specific law, public-sector AI rules beyond the strategy and code, AI procurement guidance, AI security guidance, algorithm register, national AI standard adoption, government AI readiness index, generative AI guidance or AI treaty signature was found; the UNESCO Recommendation is shown in the regional file. Not yet verified from the official text: the education ministry and public-sector development ministry sites, which were unavailable, and items known only from news, such as a Prime Ministry circular on AI (July 2026), a public-sector AI competency framework and national generative AI guidelines.
coverage_audit.technical_note:
Method note (original): Deep review completed on 6 October 2026. Documents were read from the Ministry of Digital Economy and Entrepreneurship and the Central Bank of Jordan. The official gazette copy of the Personal Data Protection Law and the Legislation and Opinion Bureau's search could not be read; the gazette index confirmed the publication issue. Official sources disagree on the date the Cabinet approved the AI Policy; the date in the Arabic text is recorded. The national cybersecurity centre, telecom regulator, standards body, procurement department and health and education ministries were searched, and no AI-specific instruments were found.

Coverage note (original): Searched MoDEE, Official Gazette index, lob.gov.jo, NCSC, TRC, JSMO, CBJ, Government Procurement Department, Ministries of Health and Education and the Tawasal consultation portal in Arabic and English. No AI-specific law, public-sector AI rules beyond the strategy and code, AI procurement guidance, NCSC AI security guidance, transparency/algorithm register, national AI standard adoption (e.g. ISO/IEC 42001), government-published AI readiness index, generative-AI-specific guidance or AI treaty signature was found. UNESCO's Recommendation is held in data/regional/UNESCO.json. Technical review notes: Deep review 2026-10-06. Sources read directly: modee.gov.jo PDFs (AI Policy 2020 EN, AI Strategy 2023–2027 AR/EN, Code of Ethics bilingual, draft charter, PDPL official translation and 2025 presentation, DTS 2021–2025 and 2026–2028) and cbj.gov.jo PDFs (AI Framework, Sandbox Framework). modee.gov.jo list pages paginate through ASP.NET postbacks, so only the first page of 'Legislation and policies' could be read automatically; documents were located through the ministry AI page and search. The Official Gazette PDF for Law 24/2023 on doc.pm.gov.jo (DocuWare) returned 'resource removed' to automated reading; the gazette index page for issue 5881 was read. lob.gov.jo (Legislation and Opinion Bureau) search is script-driven and was not usable. Official sources disagree on the date of Cabinet Decision 659 approving the AI Policy (Arabic charter: 20/12/2020; English charter: 20 Feb 2020; Strategy: 20/12/2022); the Arabic date is recorded. No dated official page gives the Cabinet approval date of the AI Strategy. The CBJ sandbox is technology-neutral (recorded with that caveat). Out of scope and not recorded: Electronic Transactions (amendment) Law No. 3 of 2026 (no AI provisions found), MoDEE information-security and social-media policies, Digital Inclusion Policy 2025. Sweep: no AI law, AI bill or AI-specific regulation found by 2026-10-06; no NCSC, TRC, JSMO, procurement, health or education AI instruments found. Ministry catch-up 2026-10-13 (PROTOCOL §2 ministry rule, applied after this country's deep review; one agent, 30 minutes, national ministries' own AI documents only, nothing else re-reviewed): 0 record(s) added. Ministries: Ministry of Education (schools): nothing found (moe.gov.jo unreachable; Siraj AI assistant is a project, not an instrument; Education Strategic Plan 2026-2030 held as lead). National Center for Curriculum Development: nothing AI-specific (General Curriculum Framework 2024 not AI-specific). Ministry of Higher Education and Scientific Research / Higher Education Council / HEAC: nothing found (site reachable, no AI document). Ministry of Health: no AI document; draft National Digital Health Strategy 2026-2030 on Tawasal held as lead (AI content unverified). Ministry of Justice / Judicial Council / courts / prosecution: nothing found. Ministry of Defence / Jordan Armed Forces: nothing found (royal directive on force restructuring incl. AI is not an instrument). Ministry of Finance / Income and Sales Tax Department / Jordan Customs: nothing found. Ministry of Interior / Public Security Directorate: nothing found. Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Expatriates: nothing found. Ministry of Labour / Social Security Corporation: nothing found. Agriculture, Transport, Energy and Mineral Resources (AI awareness workshop only, Jan 2026), Environment, Industry Trade and Supply, Culture, Tourism, Public Works, Investment: nothing found. Ministry of Government Communication / Media Commission: nothing found. Prime Ministry / Ministry of State for Public Sector Development (public-servant AI guidance): two leads (Prime Ministry circular on AI and national symbols, July 2026; public-sector AI competency framework, 2026), no official text online. MoDEE guidelines and standards list re-checked: no new AI guideline (national GenAI guidelines with ESCWA not published).. Not reached: Ministry of Education site (moe.gov.jo): connection reset / HTTP 503 via curl and WebFetch; Ministry of State for Public Sector Development site (mopsd.gov.jo): connection refused by proxy; Tawasal consultation portal listings (script-loaded; could not list consultations). Could not verify: Prime Ministry circular on AI and national symbols (July 2026): only news coverage; not on pm.gov.jo; Public-sector AI competency framework (2026): only news coverage and progress-report mentions; Draft National Digital Health Strategy 2026-2030: AI content not checked (Tawasal text not retrievable); Education Strategic Plan 2026-2030: moe.gov.jo unreachable; National generative AI guidelines (MoDEE with ESCWA consultations): no published text found on modee.gov.jo.

Catch-up sweep 2026-10-19: checked MoDEE news (to 14 Oct 2026: AI hackathon, investment delegation, Arab Digital Economy Index ranking, AI computing platform launch 15 Sep - no governance document), MoDEE public consultations page (no new AI item listed), NCSC news (to 18 Oct: recruitment, MoU), CBJ circulars page and lob.gov.jo (no text returned); found nothing new; ruled out nothing (no claims assigned); not reached: cbj.gov.jo circular list and lob.gov.jo (pages returned no readable text).

leads.english_title: Prime Ministry circular on not using AI to create or alter national emblems and symbols
leads.note: Reported in July 2026 (Al Mamlaka TV, 11 July 2026) as a government circular binding ministries, departments, public institutions, official universities, municipalities and government-owned companies: bars using AI tools to generate or alter flags, sovereign symbols, official images and seals and to publish such altered versions; allows AI for drafting, analysis and presentation. No official text found on pm.gov.jo (official statements archive lists numbered بلاغات only; Nos. 12 and 13 of 2026 are unrelated). Promote if an official copy with a stated date is found; would be administrative_policy_mandatory_in_scope (public-sector, generative-ai). 2026-10-22: Wave 3 (2026-10-22): re-searched; only Al Mamlaka TV (news/204318) and Al Khaleej (11 Jul 2026) reports found. No official text on pm.gov.jo located; keep as lead.
